permutationLabel: RIF pain labelled appendicitis, pregnancy status unknown (base case)
summary: 27-year-old woman, 20 h RIF pain referred as '?appendicitis', LMP 7 weeks ago, spotting, right shoulder-tip pain, pre-syncope, HR 112, BP 102/64; no pregnancy test yet.

inputs.hpi: 20 hours of right lower abdominal pain, referred as '?appendicitis'. Last menstrual period 7 weeks ago (usually regular). Light vaginal spotting for 2 days. Pain in the right shoulder tip when lying flat. Felt light-headed and nearly fainted when standing this morning. No fever.

exam.abdomen: Tender in the right iliac fossa and suprapubic region with guarding. No mass.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected ectopic pregnancy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right iliac fossa pain with 7 weeks' amenorrhoea, spotting, shoulder-tip pain and pre-syncope: ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise. Pregnancy test now, transvaginal ultrasound, emergency gynaecology.

socratesAnswers.lmp: 7 weeks ago — missed period; spotting for 2 days

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web: PANE top 3: cholecystitis, appendicitis, choledocholithiasis. The template's 'lmp' answer ('7 weeks ago — missed period') is not mapped to missed_period, and amenorrhoea/spotting are not SOCRATES-extracted. Symptom inference ranks ectopic #1.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Map the CC template's 'lmp' answer (missed/late period, weeks since LMP) and 'spotting' to missed_period/abnormal_uterine_bleeding PANE features.

emergencyLevel.note: Shoulder-tip pain, pre-syncope and tachycardia suggest haemoperitoneum: immediate emergency assessment.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Right lower abdominal pain' gives 'routine'.

mustInclude.note: Mandatory in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain.

mustExclude.note: No pregnancy test has been done; a template asserting 'β-HCG confirmed negative' can let an ectopic go to theatre as 'appendicitis'.

guideline.name: NICE NG126 — ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: Pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain; transvaginal ultrasound; immediate referral if haemodynamically unstable; surgical management of ruptured ectopic; anti-D
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG126, 2019 (updated 2023).

rationale: Dangerous mimic of appendicitis. A pregnancy test is mandatory in a woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain; amenorrhoea, spotting and shoulder-tip pain make ectopic pregnancy the leading diagnosis.
